author.name: Reuven Schnaider
author.headline: Senior Project Manager | Healthcare Interoperability | FHIR | AI | Digital Health Innovation

comments.text:
This is a very interesting direction, especially for reducing the “clipboard problem” in healthcare.
My main concern is less about the technical conversion itself, and more about the governance around it.
When AI converts PDFs, screenshots, or HTML forms into FHIR Questionnaires, two risks become critical:

1. Security & privacy - making sure no PHI is exposed to unauthorized AI services, prompts, logs, or intermediate storage.

2. AI hallucinations - a Questionnaire can be FHIR-valid but still clinically wrong: incorrect skip logic, invented fields, wrong terminology mapping, or assumptions that were not in the source form.

In healthcare, especially in complex domains like oncology, the output should be treated as a draft that requires strong validation, auditability, and clinical review.
FHIR-valid is not the same as clinically safe.
